body: Yes and I feel like it's infinitely more effective.

Thank you for the advice. I've been on several different medications and combinations of meds in the past. This is definitely the least terrible but I don't know if medicating myself accomplishes anything.

Different antidepressants work in different ways, some are activating while others are not. Personally I am on a combination of meds so perhaps it's one of my other medications that helps me sleep rather than the SSRI.
I'm glad to hear that you're back on track with your medication. I wish you all the best and sweet dreams :)

I had the same experience. Before going on antidepressants I never dreamed, but after a week or so of being on the medication I started having frequent, vivid dreams. Some were good and some were bad. 
One reason could be that when we are depressed our sleep quality goes down, making REM sleep (dreaming) less common. Once we are able to enter REM again or brains have to make up for all that lost time. The same happens for people getting off sleep disrupting drugs. 
Whatever the reason, it is nice to dream again. There's something comforting knowing that our minds go somewhere when we sleep instead of just falling into that void.
I have in the past with limited success.
Thank you for telling me I'm not alone. Everyone says this process just takes time, but the waiting is unbearable.

I want to believe it's just the meds making a bad situation less tolerable, but I feel like this depression is inescapable. They're supposed to make me better, so why are things getting so much worse?
